quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you:

options.text: Must let other traffic go first if they are close enough to cause a crash.
Must yield only to vehicles on your right.
Should slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must let other traffic go first if they are close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, you must let traffic already in the intersection go first. You should be ready to stop, but you can go if no other traffic is coming.

questions.question: Which statement is true about large trucks?

options.text: They need more distance to stop than passenger cars.
They all have air brakes that stop them quickly.
They are easier to steer than passenger cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more distance to stop than passenger cars.
questions.explanation: Large trucks take much longer to stop than passenger cars at the same speed. A car traveling at 55 mph can stop in about 400 feet. A truck at the same speed needs almost 800 feet.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:

options.text: Intersection.
Road curve.
Right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions just ahead. This sign warns you that another road crosses the highway ahead.

questions.question: You should not enter an intersection if you will block it when the light turns red:

options.text: Under any circumstances.
Unless you entered on a yellow light.
Unless you entered on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under any circumstances.
questions.explanation: Even if the light is green, do not enter the intersection unless you can drive all the way across before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: A round sign always warns of a railroad crossing ahead.

questions.question: A double solid yellow line down the center of a road means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A double yellow line means no one can cross it to pass, no matter which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, start from:

options.text: Any lane (if it is safe).
The lane closest to the left curb.
The center lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street, always start from the far left lane.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: Mirrors on both sides eliminate blind spots.
Large trucks have larger blind spots than most cars.
You can see all blind spots in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have larger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have very large blind spots that other drivers should avoid.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:

options.text: Oncoming traffic traveling straight or turning right.
Passing cars.
No one in particular.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming traffic traveling straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must let all oncoming traffic go first. This includes cars, motorcycles, and bicycles.

questions.question: If you see a severe dust storm, you should:

options.text: Slow down and drive off the road.
Turn on your high beams.
Keep your speed and stay in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive off the road.
questions.explanation: In a severe dust storm, slow down and drive completely off the highway as far to the right as possible. Turn off your lights, keep your foot off the brake, stay in your car with your seat belt on, and wait for the storm to pass.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Saves time and gets you there quicker.
Helps you avoid obstacles.
Increases the risk of serious injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of serious injury and death.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to dangerous driving choices.

questions.question: When a school bus is stopped to load or unload children, you must:

options.text: Stop completely until all children leave the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is raised.
Change lanes and pass the bus slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is raised.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and a stop arm extended, you must stop completely. Do not go until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is raised. Make sure no children are crossing the road before you proceed.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, it is safe to return to your lane if you:

options.text: Cannot see the vehicle next to you on the right.
See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
Have passed the vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane after passing, make sure you have enough distance from the other vehicle. When you can see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough space to move back safely.

questions.question: When parking at a curb, use your turn signals:

options.text: Only when leaving the curb.
Only when pulling next to the curb.
When pulling next to or leaving the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling next to or leaving the curb.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signals both when parking at a curb and when leaving a curb.

questions.question: Drivers must obey instructions from:

options.text: Security guards in parking lots.
Other drivers whose cars are broken down on the road.
Flaggers at construction sites.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flaggers at construction sites.
questions.explanation: You must follow the signals and instructions from flaggers at construction sites. They are there to keep drivers and workers safe.

questions.question: To see vehicles in your blind spots, you should check:

options.text: The inside rearview mirror.
The outside rearview mirror.
Over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over your shoulders to check your blind spots.

questions.question: When a car with bright headlights drives toward you at night, you should:

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes.
Look below their headlights.
Glance toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Glance toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at bright headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, you should:

options.text: Activate your turn signal.
Reduce your speed.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: You may drive slower than the posted speed limit based on road conditions. Reduce speed for curves, hills, slippery roads, and areas with pedestrians or animals.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
Keep a steady pace.
Stay in the driver's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not drive in someone's blind spot. Move ahead or fall back so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Pass the vehicle as slowly as possible.
Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.
Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Pass quickly to get back to your lane safely. Return to your lane only when you can see both of the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must travel through the intersection at the posted speed limit.
The maximum speed limit under ideal conditions is 55 mph.
You must not travel below the speed indicated.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed limit under ideal conditions is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum speed limit for that road. You may drive slower based on conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, it is safe to return to your driving lane when:

options.text: The driver you passed signals for you to return to your lane.
You signal your intention for three seconds.
You see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Look in your rearview mirror to make sure you have enough space. When you see both headlights of the vehicle you passed, you can return to your lane.

questions.question: If the rear of your vehicle is skidding to the left, you should:

options.text: Not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.
Turn your steering wheel to the right to correct the skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.
questions.explanation: If you skid on a wet or icy road, take your foot off the accelerator, avoid braking, and steer in the direction of the skid. If you have anti-lock brakes, brake firmly and steer straight ahead.

questions.question: In heavy fog, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Turn your lights to their high beam setting.
Turn your lights to their low beam setting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your lights to their low beam setting.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights for additional help.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means:

options.text: The same thing as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same thing as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.
Slow-moving vehicle.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for vehicles with disability license plates or disability parking placards.

questions.question: A pentagon-shaped sign is a:

options.text: Stop sign.
Regulatory sign.
School zone or school crossing sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone or school crossing sign.
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign warns drivers about school zones. It alerts you that children and pedestrians may be nearby.

questions.question: Driving slower than surrounding traffic is:

options.text: A good idea if the weather is bad.
Appropriate if you don't know the speed limit.
Often a hazard because other drivers may become frustrated and try to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often a hazard because other drivers may become frustrated and try to pass you.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic can be dangerous. Drivers behind you may become impatient and take risky actions to pass you.

questions.question: If you are driving near a large commercial vehicle, you should:

options.text: Follow the large vehicle closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.
Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.
questions.explanation: Large commercial vehicles have large blind spots on both sides. Do not drive beside them for long periods of time.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, you should:

options.text: Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.
Use your high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.
Use your high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.
questions.explanation: Use high beams only in rural areas when no other cars are nearby. Switch to low beams when you are following another vehicle.
